title: Take the pricing rules out of the allocation profile

blocks.text: The checkout service prices every order line through rules named in configuration: a rule is any object with a public `int apply(int cents)`, registered at startup with `add(name, rule)`. Since the rules were added, the allocation profile of a busy checkout node shows `java.lang.Integer` as its top allocated type, with the stacks ending in the rule table, and young-generation GCs have doubled.
Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/RuleTable.java`: `prepare(rule)` turns one rule object into the `IntUnaryOperator` that `apply(name, cents)` calls for it.
When you're done, every name applies its own rule object, an object without `int apply(int)` is refused when it is added, and applying a rule allocates nothing. About ten lines in total.
The tests measure allocation with the thread's allocation counter, over amounts well outside the `Integer` cache.

cases.says: each name applies the rule object registered under it
an object without an int apply(int) is refused with IllegalArgumentException when it is added
two rule objects of the same class each apply their own settings
applying a rule to amounts outside the Integer cache allocates no objects

origin.section: A Method Handle Obeys the Same Rule, and invokeExact Never Boxes

concepts: Method.invoke boxes each int argument and result outside the Integer cache, and escape analysis removes only the argument array; a handle bound to its receiver and called with invokeExact allocates nothing.
